title: SDK Flow Pipelines & Sequence Telemetry — PRD draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact PRD for two tightly coupled capabilities in the Hosted API surface: (1) an SDK-oriented flow/pipeline abstraction for low-latency streaming + tool-calling, and (2) sequence-level telemetry to make per-request performance and quality signals actionable for engineers and product teams. Goal is to ship initial beta in Hosted API + SDK (JS + Python) that lets product teams instrument and operate streaming+tool patterns with clear fallback semantics, minimal client complexity, and observability hooks for regressions.

Background and motivation:
- Existing hosted streaming primitives (chunked token delivery) are widely used but leak complexity into client apps when tool-calling, partial structured outputs, and retries/fallbacks are combined.
- Operators and SREs need sequence-aware telemetry (not just per-token or per-request totals) to detect regressions introduced by rollout, quantization, or kernel changes.
- SDKs should offer a small set of composable flow primitives (pipeline stages) so teams can implement: optimistic-tool-invoke, confirm-on-completion, fallback-to-model, and reranking with predictable latency/ cost tradeoffs.

Success metrics (first 3 months post-beta):
- Developer adoption: 30+ internal services integrate SDK flow primitives for streaming-tool patterns.
- Latency: 90th percentile end-to-end latency for “tool-first” flows <= baseline + 25ms for same model/region.
- Observability adoption: 80% of integrated services emit sequence-telemetry spans for streaming requests.
- Incident reduction: reduce ambiguous streaming-tool incidents (where root cause unknown) by 50% via clearer telemetry.

User stories:
- Marcus (Search PM): Wants deterministic behavior when an external retriever is called mid-stream. If retriever fails, the app must continue with a model-only fallback without duplicating partial outputs to the customer.
- Priya (Conversational AI engineer): Needs typed partial outputs (JSON fragments) with an SDK-level commit/cancel API so UI only renders complete structured results.
- SRE (oncall): Needs sequence-level traces that show when a request hit cache, used a dedicated pool, or fell back to CPU quantized variant, and how many tokens were generated per stage.

Key concepts and non-goals:
- Sequence pipeline: an ordered list of stages executed for a single high-level request. Example stages: client-validate -> prefix-cache -> model-stream -> tool-invoke -> confirm-commit -> post-process.
- Stage contracts: each stage returns (event-stream, terminal-status). Event-stream = ordered events (partial_text, structured_chunk, tool_call, tool_result, error, end). Terminal-status = success|fallback|error|cancelled.
- Telemetry units: sequence-id, stage-id, stage-latency-ms, tokens-produced, bytes-sent, fallback-reason, model-variant, backend-pool, trace-id.
- Non-goal: This PRD will not design new server-side routing policies (that is separate). It focuses on SDK surface, protocol, and telemetry shape.

SDK flow API sketches (consumer ergonomic goals):
- Composeable, minimal surface area, explicit commit/cancel, easy opt-in to telemetry.
- Single streaming connection per sequence for low overhead.
- Clear semantics for tool calls: optimistic vs conservative modes.

Example (JS pseudocode, high-level):

const seq = client.startSequence({model: 'rw-large-v1', telemetry: true});
seq.on('partial', (p) => ui.append(p.text));
seq.on('structured', (obj) => buffer.objPart(obj));

// optimistic tool call: SDK sends tool_call event to server while continuing tokens
seq.callTool('qa_retriever', {query: q}, {mode: 'optimistic', timeoutMs: 300})
  .then((result) => seq.injectToolResult(result))
  .catch((err) => seq.applyFallback('retriever-failed'));
// commit only when structured output is complete
await seq.commitIf(() => buffer.isComplete());

// cancellation
seq.cancel('user-abort');

Primitives exposed:
- startSequence(opts) -> SequenceHandle (id, events, telemetry toggle)
- SequenceHandle.on(event, handler)  // events: partial, structured, tool_call_request, tool_result, metrics
- callTool(name, args, options) -> Promise  // options: mode: optimistic|blocking, deadline, idempotency_key
- injectToolResult(toolResult)  // for deterministic replay or simulated results in tests
- commitIf(predicate) / commit() / cancel(reason)

Modes for tool-calling and expected semantics:
- optimistic: continue streaming tokens while tool call is in flight; SDK must ensure duplicate tokens are deduplicated if tool result later inserts structured content. Useful for low-latency UX but requires client to support insertion/repair of UI.
- blocking: pause token emission until tool returns; simpler for client but increases latency.
- speculative: SDK can speculatively call multiple tools and select earliest high-confidence result.

Sequence-level telemetry shape (proposal):
- sequence_id: string
- start_ts, end_ts
- stages: list of stage-id tokens (see below; flattened in telemetry row as repeated fields)
- for each stage (stage_id, type, start_ts, end_ts, latency_ms, tokens_out, model_variant, pool, fallback_reason if any)
- events: list of important events with timestamps (tool_call_sent, tool_response_received, commit, cancel, error)
- quality_signals: optional (bleu/rerank_score/human_eval_id)

Implementation notes (server + SDK interactions):
- Sequence id is issued by server at handshake; SDK attaches trace-id for distributed tracing.
- Events stream is protobuf/JSON events over the streaming channel. Each event includes stage_id and cumulative token index to allow deterministic alignment client-side.
- To avoid large memory blowups, structured_chunk events can be chunked with seq offsets.
- Server emits telemetry span for each stage; SDK emits a small summary envelope at end of sequence to reduce cardinality on the ingestion path if user enables telemetry=true.

Backward compatibility strategy:
- Default to present behavior if SDK opts out.
- Telemetry and stage metadata are opt-in via client parameter; events remain human-readable to avoid brittle parsing by older clients.

Operational scenarios and fallback semantics:
1) Retriever fails (tool timed out): if callTool(mode=optimistic) -> server emits tool_failed event, SDK applies applyFallback('tool-timeout') which triggers server-side continuation using model-only branch. Telemetry marks stage terminal-status=fallback with fallback_reason=tool-timeout.
2) Tool returns inconsistent structured JSON: SDK can surface validation errors as structured events and either cancel sequence (commit=false) or attempt model re-generation; this is configurable per-sequence.
3) Partial commit after tool: allow partial commit for conversational flows where tool result adds metadata (e.g., sources) but partial text should be shown earlier. SDK exposes commit granularity (text-only commit vs structured commit).

Observability and UI:
- Console: new per-sequence timeline view: horizontal swimlanes for stages, with tool-call boxes and hoverable metrics (latency, tokens).
- Alerts: regression detectors based on tokens-per-stage, fraction of sequences using fallback, and mean tool latency.
- Querying: support search by sequence_id, trace_id, service, model_variant.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much work to push to SDK vs server for deduping optimistic tokens? (SDK simpler to evolve but increases client complexity)
- Cardinality risk for telemetry fields (model_variant vs pool vs commit-mode). Need sampling and envelope summarization.
- Semantics for speculative multi-tool calls (conflict resolution policy).

Implementation roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- Q1 (beta): API sketches in JS/Python SDKs, server event protocol v1, basic telemetry envelope ingestion and console timeline prototype.
- Q2 (stability): Add commit granularity, tool-call modes in server, telemetry enrichers (pool/model variant), internal dogfood + feedback.
- Q3 (GA): Metrics-driven rollout, SDK ergonomics polish, on-by-default telemetry for enterprise customers with SLAs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Complexity for client engineers: provide drop-in higher-level helpers (e.g., useOptimisticTool(seq, toolOpts)) and ship good samples + React/Flutter UI patterns.
- Telemetry cost: compress and summarize per-sequence and sample heavy sequences; offer toggles for retention.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: implement server handshake and event schema (ENG-1423) — owner: Ravi Singh — due: 2026-01-15
- SDK: ship JS prototype and tests for optimistic/blocking modes — owner: Emily Park — due: 2026-01-30
- Product: prepare console prototype for sequence timeline — owner: Marta Alvarez — due: 2026-02-12
- SRE: define alert thresholds and telemetry quotas — owner: Jonas Müller — due: 2026-02-05

Notes to reviewers:
- Please focus review on the Stage contract (events and terminal-status) and the telemetry field list — these are high leverage for both client ergonomics and backend cost.
- Call out any existing internal SDK patterns we should reuse rather than re-invent (e.g., existing connection pooling, backpressure APIs).

Roughly related tickets and references (internal):
- ENG-1423: sequence telemetry event schema (proto)
- OPT-298: SDK tool-calling ergonomics spike
- PR#4532: initial JS SDK streaming-handler (prototype)

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Finalize event wire format (JSON vs compact protobuf) for telemetry envelope.
- Author test matrix for optimistic tool failure modes.
- UX patterns: partial-UI repair behavior examples for optimistic insertions.

End of draft.
